summary: Pass. r1's block (sidecar vs automatic gate edits) is resolved: the content key excludes phase/updated, which is all gate touches, and the test "publish, gate phase edit, publish" covers it. r1 warns are also resolved: fresh clone now has the `plan pull` path, `body_section` is gated on the base pin against PLAN_COMMENT_SINCE (a too-high guess fails safe, since consumers stay on "required"), the workflow is justified with a narrow trust boundary, and a missing label is created rather than failing. Remaining defects are warns: gate's own-login-only upsert conflicts with the any-writer plan comment, and the behaviour when truncation removes the data block is undefined. Order is shippable: step 1 is independent, PR A ships the section as optional before sessions stop writing it, then PR B. Security controls are well placed: collaborators API writer check, line-1 parsing via env, no PR checkout, and the never-on-page filter before the first post and every edit.

findings.note: The plan writes the live plan comment from `gate plan`/`gate publish`, but the existing gate.ts upsertOwnComment only edits comments authored by the caller's own login, while line 25 lets any writer's newest comment be the plan; a plan posted by another login or the cloud proxy makes the gate phase PATCH fail or need new lookup code, so state that gate uses the plan-comment finder and warns on a 403.

Truncation drops the data block first, but the line-26 concurrency check reads the content key from that block; define what publish does when the live comment has no data block (refuse and name `plan pull`, or treat the key as unknown), or a truncated plan makes every later publish either falsely refuse or silently overwrite.
The one-line pointer left on the issue after a move must not carry the `boonty-plan/v1` marker on line 1, or the writer-newest rule and the pr-status workflow will treat the pointer as the plan.
The read-compare-PATCH in publish has a small race window between the live read and the write; acceptable for this threat model, but say it is best-effort.
